top.title: Fifpro criticises Bayern Munich for Musiala comments
top.description: Musiala joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy [Getty Images] Football players' union Fifpro says it is concerned by comments from Bayern Munich's hierarchy about Jamal Musiala's contract, adding the German club "should know better". Musiala collapsed twice in four days during pre-season and the 23-year-old Germany international said he had been diagnosed with "easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction". Bayern honorary president Uli Hoeness said earlier this month Musiala may never "regain the performance level he once had" . The Bundesliga club's chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also questioned the lucrative contract extension the forward signed in 2025, running until 2030, if Musiala fails to get back to his best form, while his predecessor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has suggested the deal may need to be renegotiated. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. "In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better." Musiala may never return to his best - Hoeness Two collapses in four days - what's happening to Musiala? Musiala, who joined Bayern in 2019 after coming through Chelsea's academy, came on for the German champions after 70 minutes in a 1-1 draw with Cologne on Friday as he made his first outing since scoring in a 7-0 win against Union Berlin on 18 September. He has made five appearances for the club this season, scoring two goals and providing one assist. "Bayern has a duty of care to Musiala," added Fifpro. "Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Any concerns about his contract should be raised privately with him and his representatives. "Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise." Musiala's return to the Bayern side came in the same game in which England striker Harry Kane suffered an ankle injury and was subsequently ruled out "for the next few months". Former Baltimore Ravens safety Bernard Pollard has raised concerns about the organization’s fading defensive identity and Lamar Jackson ’s future amid trade speculation as the team prepares for its Week 11 road matchup against the Carolina Panthers. With the Ravens (4-6) looking to snap a five-game losing streak against the Panthers (4-5) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, Pollard believes Baltimore has strayed from the defensive standard that defined the franchise for decades. In a recent interview with Kyle Odegard of RotoGrinders, Pollard criticized the team’s defensive struggles and questioned whether its personnel and coaching staff have maintained that identity. They need to hold the players accountable to that, while bringing in players who hold each other accountable.” Baltimore’s defense has surrendered 2,306 passing yards and 1,059 rushing yards, including a league-high 14 rushing touchdowns. top.title: Jorge Martin on keeping MotoGP title hopes alive: ‘I didn’t do anything, it was in Marquez’s hands’
top.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin admitted that he lacked speed in the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint, suggesting he owes his slim MotoGP title hopes entirely to Marc Marquez ’s crash. The factory Aprilia rider arrived at Portimao needing to outscore Marquez by 24 points over the weekend to take the championship fight to the Valencia finale. But after qualifying five places behind Marquez in seventh, Martin failed to make any headway in the sprint, gaining only one position in the opening 10 laps. That would have let Marquez seal the title with a third-place finish, but the Ducati star crashed out of the sprint on the penultimate tour as rain began to fall on the track. Speaking afterwards, Martin admitted that he was lagging behind the frontrunners at Portimao, particularly with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi converting pole position into a dominant win. Asked whether he had kept his championship hopes alive, Martin insisted the outcome was never in his hands given the points situation. “Well, I didn't ‘keep’ anything. Everything was in Marc's hands,” he said. “For sure, it was a really tricky race. I didn't have the speed all weekend. Finally, in the race, it seemed I found a little bit extra. I was quite close to the podium fight, but I missed a bit more speed. “But in the end, I did my best. I finished in fifth position. Let's hope for a bigger improvement tomorrow. “When the conditions are really tricky like this, the focus more goes on riding because you need to be at 100%. “So you don't have room to think about anything. I was just really focused. I tried to fight the first few laps with Pedro [Acosta], trying to go in the front, and he was a bit faster. “We were catching the riders in front a bit, so this is good. I saw the places where I'm a bit slower, the places where I'm a bit faster than him.” Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Marquez has shown remarkable consistency since he returned from injury at the Italian Grand Prix in May, avoiding the kind of mistakes that have plagued Bezzecchi and Martin’s campaigns. The reigning world champion himself noted that his crash out of the sprint was his first real mistake in the second half of the season, coming just a day after he warned about the risks of racing with the title within reach. Martin said he understood why Marquez made an error at such a crucial stage of the championship, particularly with the weather conditions changing at Portimao. “Surprised? No. In these tricky conditions, anything can happen. “When you are in front, I can understand his position. Everything gets more risky, everything gets more stiff, as he said yesterday. “The problem for him was he wasn't alone at that point. I was behind Marc and Alex [Marquez]. So I saw the crash and then I relaxed a bit in that corner. Otherwise, maybe I would [also] crash. “So, this is racing and a bit unlucky. I thought he was going to make it [win the championship], honestly. So it was incredible. “I have another chance tomorrow, but anyway

top.description: Post-match reaction from Celtic scorers after Paradise win Celtic’s midfield required some personnel changes this afternoon, with both Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur ruled out through injury. top.title: Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them
top.description: Jul 22, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; former Alabama Crimson Tide coach and ESPN analyst for College GameDay Nick Saban broadcast during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images With just a couple of weeks left in the regular season, the College Football Playoff picture is starting to come into focus. And one of the most decorated coaches in the sport’s history thinks that only a few teams have what it takes to win it all. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban said on Friday that there are “three teams that have the right stuff” to win the national championship: Georgia, Utah, and Notre Dame. And despite spending more than two decades coaching in the SEC, he made sure to clarify that it was “no disrespect to Alabama.” Playoff Picture Taking Shape Georgia sits at No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings at 9-1, with its only loss coming against Auburn in October. The Bulldogs have won three straight since then, including a 48-21 win over Missouri last weekend. Utah is right behind at No. 2 and is one of two undefeated teams in the top five at 10-0, along with No. 4 UCLA, though the Utes needed a 40-39 win at Arizona last weekend to keep their perfect season alive. Notre Dame checks in at No. 6 at 9-1, with its only loss coming at BYU. The Fighting Irish have since won three straight, including a 31-24 win over Miami. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr were both named finalists for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award on Friday, according to On3. On the same show, Saban insisted that the SEC is still the best conference from top to bottom, despite the Big Ten winning three straight national titles. Yet only one of his three contenders plays in the SEC. ‘The right stuff’ Saban shared his picks during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think there’s three teams that have the right stuff. And this is no disrespect to Alabama, because I think there’s probably seven to eight teams that can win the championship, Alabama being one of them. But if you’re a betting man and you say, ‘OK, who can run the ball, who can play good defense and who has a good quarterback?’ You would say Georgia has that, Utah has that, Notre Dame has that,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban added that the rest of the contenders have weaknesses that could hold them back. “Everybody else maybe has a flaw somewhere along the way. Now they might be able to overcome it, but I think those three teams have the right stuff,” Saban said. That leaves out Alabama, which the committee has ranked No. 3, as well as No. 4 UCLA, No. 5 Texas, and No. 7 Miami, among others. Clearly, Saban thinks the national title race is a lot narrower than the rankings suggest. top.title: Redick Fires Up Lakers After Listless First Half vs. Kings
top.description: May 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick yells to his team during a play against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the first half during game two of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images The Lakers did not look like a championship team for the first 24 minutes on Friday. They looked flat against the last-place Sacramento Kings, trailing by eight points at the break. Coach JJ Redick had seen enough and decided to get loud . He did not sugarcoat the message to his squad in the locker room. “I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime… They may have a differing opinion of that. Can’t repeat every word I used,” Redick said after the team secured a narrow 106-104 win . The coach admitted his words were harsh but necessary to wake the players up. A Wake-Up Call for the Big Men Redick’s anger was not aimed at everyone equally. He zeroed in on center Walker Kessler , who had just six points, one rebound, and four fouls before the break. The coach told Kessler to be tougher and bring some energy. Kessler did not argue with the approach, noting that Reddick tore into him about it, and rightfully so. The player admitted he was not playing physically or going to the rim. He needed that push to find his game. Kessler finished with 15 points and seven rebounds after the halftime talk. He credited the coach for knowing when to yell. The contrast between the two big men was stark. While Kessler struggled early, Kings star Domantas Sabonis dominated with 15 points and eight boards. The Lakers could not let that happen again. Redick made sure they understood the stakes. “The main message was we’ve got to be tougher, we’ve got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick explained. He noted that some players might have a different opinion of his halftime speech. He would not repeat every word he used, but the point was clear. Stars Back the Coach’s Approach Even the biggest stars on the roster agreed with the coach’s methods. Luka Doncic led the team with 25 points and eight assists. He said the yelling helped get everyone fired up. “I mean, he yells, but I’m used to it,” Doncic said. He noted that sometimes it is good to have a coach who demands more. The team managed to outscore Sacramento 52-42 over the final two quarters. That second-half surge kept them from losing to a team with a 1-14 record. The game came down to the final second. Sacramento guard Zach LaVine had a chance to win it with a three-pointer at the buzzer. The shot clanked off the front rim, and the Lakers survived. The win lifted L.A. to 14-3 on the season. It was their second win in NBA Cup games. The victory was sweet, but the performance was far from perfect . The team has now survived close calls against weaker opponents all week. Per ESPN , the Lakers needed a 47-point night from Quentin Grimes to beat the Hornets on Tuesday. Redick knows that scraping by is not enough for a top seed.

top.title: ‘There’s a bigger issue people just don’t get’: Metta World Peace claps back after Stephen A. Smith’s racial Laker comments
top.description: Jan 7, 2020; Los Angeles, California, USA; Metta World Peace (Ron Artest) attends a game between the Los Angeles Lakers and the New York Knicks at Staples Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Los Angeles Lakers sit at the top of the Western Conference at 14-3, just ahead of the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs, despite losing superstar veteran LeBron James. European sensation Luka Doncic has firmly secured the reins of the team and is aiming to be an NBA scoring champ at the pace he’s playing. But the new roster selection has received criticism from some of sports’ most acclaimed commentators despite their hot start. After James left in free agency this offseason, the Lakers’ new-look roster drew plenty of reaction, especially from ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith, who couldn’t picture three white guys winning an NBA title in today’s league. But between Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler, the trio has averaged 76.2 points, 20.8 rebounds, and 14.2 assists per game. Recently, on First Take , Smith doubled down on his thoughts while openly asking “the brothers” around the league to step up and stop the Lakers, creating a media spiral of its own . Wednesday, former Lakers champion Metta World Peace pushed back against Smith’s take, making it clear he has zero issue with a white-run team. “I love seeing white basketball players on same team,” World Peace wrote via X . “I feel no less insecure about a majority white @Lakers. That’s like saying you are afraid of a black mom and black dad born president. People are so unaware that they are ignitors of racism. That’s like saying, my new semi chip company will not succeed because I’m a black board member. Let the white ball players rock and let our future black financial system principals and my new social impact go to market concepts rock.” Friday, in a video posted by Bassey on X , World Peace continued to defend his positioning but deepened the outlook as he believes there are other underlying issues that have been “brewing for years” in the NBA. “There’s a bigger issue that people just don’t get in terms of us players that are dope in sports. We charge for training,” World Peace added. “So now one of the issues is that a lot of us that’s out of poverty cannot afford even our services that came from poverty, which is why we do a lot of free work. So there are a lot of, you know, ethnic, you know, kind of, cultured individuals of the same ethnicity as myself that’s not getting the same training, because they can’t afford it.” It is not unusual for Smith’s comments to cause such an uproar, but his reaction will be interesting to see given that he has had a heavy political schedule for the past few months. top.title: Nikhil Chaudhary shines as Australia beat England in thrilling first T20I to take 1-0 lead
top.description: Nikhil Chaudhary produced a memorable all-round performance as Australia edged past England in a thrilling final-over finish in the opening T20I at the MCG to take a 1-0 lead in the series. Chasing 188 for victory, Australia held their nerve despite losing wickets at regular intervals, with Chaudhary and Jack Edwards playing decisive roles in getting the hosts across the line. Australia suffered an early setback when Jake Fraser-McGurk departed for just one in the opening over. However, debutant Sam Harper provided an immediate spark, smashing 32 off just 15 deliveries to give the hosts a flying start in the powerplay. Captain Mitchell Marsh contributed 37 off 32 balls but struggled to maintain the scoring momentum as England attempted to claw their way back into the contest. With wickets falling at the other end, Chaudhary took charge of the chase. He first stitched together a valuable 42-run stand with Marsh before combining with Tim David, who scored 20 off 13 deliveries. The duo added 48 runs in just 29 balls to keep Australia firmly on course. Chaudhary continued to find the boundaries and hold the innings together, but his dismissal brought pressure on the hosts. top.title: Oregon men's cross country misses NCAA podium by single point
top.description: The Oregon men fell one-point short of ending their long NCAA Cross Country Championships trophy drought. Led by a pair of all-American performances from Nick Griggs and Simeon Birnbaum, the Ducks scored 196 points as a team to finish in fifth place Nov. 21 at on the LaVern Gibson Championship Course in Terre Haute, Ind. BYU was fourth with 195 points, leaving Oregon off the podium for an 11th straight year. Griggs made his Ducks’ and NCAA debut Saturday, finishing the 10,000-meter race in ninth place in 28:45.7. Birnbaum was 23rd in 29:05.1. Oregon’s next scorer was Myles Hogan, who was 65th in 29:36.5, followed by Aiden Smith, who was 70th in 29:41.0 and Benjamin Balazs, who was 79th in 29:48.4. Also on the course for the Ducks were Tayson Echohawk (93rd in 29:57.4) and Evan Jenkins (205th in 31:00.0). Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto took home the individual title with a 28:27.7 finish. New Mexico, with three runners finishing in the top 10 and four in the top 14, won the team title with 69 points. Colorado was second with 107 and Alabama third with 109. Oregon women finish ninth The Ducks had a pair of finishers in the top 25, but there was a big gap between them and their other scorers as Oregon scored 312 points to finish in ninth place. Diana Cherotich was Oregon’s top runner as the Big Ten champ finished the 6,000-meter race in 17th place in 19:06.8. Juliet Cherubet wasn’t far behind as she finished in 21st in 19:10.9. Both runners earned all-American status – a third such honor for Cherubet and second for Cherotich. Dalia Frias finished in 58th (19:37.3), Ella Thorsett was 108th (20:08.8) and Ava Parekh was 185th (20:46.5). Finishing outside of scoring was Kendall Martin, who was 246th in 21:34.9. Sofia Thogersen, who had been the Ducks’ No. 4 runner all season, started but didn’t finish the race. Hannah Grapes of NC State was the individual winner in 18:44.3. Alabama won the team title with 120 points, West Virginia was second at 145, BYU was third with 152, and Northern Arizona was fourth with 215. top.title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence falls to 12% as frustration reaches new low
top.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to an NFL football game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction . That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have little belief in the current direction of the franchise. The continued decline in confidence is hardly surprising. The Colts have spent the past several weeks spiraling, and whatever optimism may have briefly surfaced after some of the front office changes has quickly disappeared. Poor offensive play, frustrating coaching decisions and the overall lack of progress from week to week have left fans with very little reason to feel encouraged. Rather than showing signs of a team building toward something, Indianapolis has looked like a franchise stuck in the middle of a messy transition. The biggest recent development, of course, is that Daniel Jones is now gone, officially closing the book on a move that never gave the Colts the boost they were hoping for. Jones had a few respectable moments early on, but the offense became increasingly dysfunctional under his watch, and it eventually reached a point where a change simply had to be made. His departure does not solve all of Indianapolis’ problems, but it does signal that the organization recognized the situation was no longer tenable. Even so, the quarterback change alone is unlikely to restore confidence overnight. The issues with this team go far beyond one player. Shane Steichen continues to face questions about the offense, the roster still has major holes, and the Colts remain far away from looking like a legitimate contender. At the same time, fans are now left wondering whether this next phase will at least provide some clarity about the future, even if the short-term results remain ugly. For now, this week’s 12 percent confidence mark says it all. Colts fans are not just frustrated, they are increasingly unconvinced that this franchise has a real plan in place. If Indianapolis wants that number to rise in the coming weeks, it will need to show something far more convincing than it has lately. top.title: Aston Villa frustrated by Sunderland in dull goalless draw
top.description: Aston Villa and Sunderland drew a blank in their Premier League match at Villa Park. Unai Emery’s team had the better of a game of few chances but failed to make the breakthrough and are now without a win in five games in all competitions. Sunderland, bidding to move away from the relegation zone, ended a run of three successive away defeats with the 0-0 draw. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Emiliano Buendia returned for Villa at the expense of Victor Lindelof and John McGinn , who was on the bench. Sunderland also made two changes, with Jules Ahoka and Wilson Isidor replacing the injured Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey. The home side were on the front foot from the off and forced a couple of early corners, which came to nothing. They had to wait until the 19th minute for their first chance, with Johan Manzambi’s low effort saved by Robin Roefs. The Sunderland goalkeeper had a let-off in the 40th minute when he gifted possession to Buendia but recovered to claim the Villa midfielder’s weak shot. Ian Maatsen threatened to break the deadlock in the early stages of the second half, but he could only follow an impressive run with a shot straight at Roefs. Soon after the Black Cats, who created little of note before half-time, forced their first corner but failed to produce anything worthwhile from it. Villa’s Leon Goretzka was then booked for pulling back Chemsdine Talbi, but Enzo Le Fee’s free-kick evaded Nordi Mukiele and was collected by goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. As Villa fans chanted for the introduction of McGinn, Le Fee fired narrowly wide. The home faithful got what they wanted just before the hour mark when McGinn was introduced, alongside Ibrahim Mbaye. The Scotland international had a chance to open the scoring midway through the second half but fired over. Sunderland won a free-kick 25 yards out when Goretzka fouled Le Fee, but the midfielder’s effort was straight at Suzuki. Villa boss Emery made another double substitution in the 73rd minute, with Brian Madjo and Ross Barkley replacing Nicolas Jackson and Goretzka. The home side pressed for a winner and, after McGinn failed to find the target three minutes later, Barkley forced Roefs to tip over a powerful effort from distance. Roefs reacted sharply to prevent Mukiele heading into his own goal, then Alysson fired over. The visitors almost stole a win in the first of three added minutes, but Talbi’s curling right-foot effort went narrowly wide of Suzuki’s far post.

top.title: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo
top.description: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo Jose Mourinho’s influence on the Real Madrid dressing room and slowly, yet surely grown, and the player now appear more hungry and prepared to win than they have in recent years. The opening phase of the season, which lasted until the first international break, saw Los Blancos adapt to Mourinho’s ways and even struggle to rack up wins. They were often dominated and scraped through games, which was understandable. After the first international break, however, matters changed for the good and the men in white began to look increasingly convincing. They began controlling games better and performing consistently, with the Clasico win marking their highest point. Phase 3 begins Mourinho has got Real Madrid back on track. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) As reported by AS in a recent update, Mourinho sees the new phase of the season that lies ahead of of the team as their third phase, and he is hoping for an even better run. By the time Christmas arrives, the manager hopes that Los Blancos are playing better football and that they have the UEFA Champions League qualification in the bag. If possible, he even hopes for a change on the league leaderboard with his side going on top. Mourinho’s plans have been moving as expected so far, but the manager is aware that the project is just getting started and that there is a long way to go. He has even proclaimed that reaching perfection will require ‘three seasons.’ Big games ahead Real Madrid have unpleasant memories of playing against Arsenal heading into next month’s clash. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Between the game against Celta Vigo tonight and the end of the year, Real Madrid have some big games to get past, and the third phase will be more challenging than one anticipates. For starters, Los Blancos will take on PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League after the clash against Celta Vigo, and will then go on a challenging three away-game streak. First, they must travel to Anoeta where they must take on Real Sociedad, and they then travel to San Mames for a clash against Real Sociedad. Both games, needless to say, are difficult outings and bring back unfavourable memories. Then, Mourinho and Co. must take on Arsenal away from home – a game that will bring back ghosts of the past. After all, they lost 3-0 at the venue – one of their biggest European defeats in recent times.

top.title: Bournemouth climb up to fourth after securing ninth victory in a row
top.description: Bournemouth extended their winning run to nine in all competitions as Evanilson scored for the sixth Premier League game in a row in a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Justin Kluivert was also on target to help Marco Rose’s Cherries climb up to the dizzying heights of fourth place in the table. The defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win over Manchester City before the international break. Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva. Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels. Bournemouth took the lead through Evanilson in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the in-form Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-footed shot into the roof of the net. Evanilson (centre) celebrates the opening goal (Steven Paston/PA) (PA Wire) Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from the edge of the penalty area which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area. Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of team-mate Tyler Adams. Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier. Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to forage a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for captain Morgan Gibbs-White but the England international could not properly connect with his header. James McAtee ballooned an effort over the crossbar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. Substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper Dorde Petrovic. Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and the Cherries’ third when he stung the gloves of Selz from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.

nigeria.description: Chelsea suffered an embarrassing 4-1 defeat against Leeds on Saturday as the Blues were beaten for the third time in their last four Premier League matches. Xabi Alonso’s side were ripped apart by rampant Leeds, who savoured their first Premier League win at Stamford Bridge in 27 years. Chelsea scored six in a League Cup win against Leeds in September, but Daniel Farke’s men erased that painful result with a superb display on their return to west London. Just 24 hours after NFL legend Tom Brady was linked with buying a minority stake in Chelsea, the seven-time Super Bowl winner might be thinking twice about his mooted investment. Brady is believed to be friendly with Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali, who will have a big decision to make on Alonso’s future if results do not improve soon. Chelsea are languishing in eighth place after a fifth defeat in their 11 league games under Alonso, who was hyped as the stabilising force the club needed after a turbulent period. Alonso has been hampered by the absence of injured Brazilian striker Joao Pedro in recent weeks and once again Chelsea struggled without their attacking talisman. Making his full debut in Alonso’s latest bid to find a stand-in for Pedro, Emmanuel Emegha fired Chelsea ahead in the 25th minute. Yet within three minutes they gifted an equaliser to Noah Okafor, who punished static defending to lash home. Morgan Rogers conceded a penalty eight minutes into the second half and Dominic Calvert-Lewin converted to put Leeds in front. Swiss striker Okafor quickly made it three in the 58th minute and Brenden Aaronson got a fourth in stoppage-time to leave Chelsea in turmoil. Over a miserable five-match spell, the Blues have lost to Tottenham, Sunderland and Leeds, while also crashing out of the League Cup against Liverpool. While it is too soon to suggest Alonso is in danger of the sack, the Spaniard has endured a disappointing start to his first spell as a Premier League manager. Failing to beat struggling pair Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two games would undoubtedly turn the heat up on the former Real Madrid and Bayer Leverkusen boss. nigeria.title: English village votes to ‘leave UK’ over migrant camp plan
nigeria.description: A small English village on Saturday voted to leave the UK in a symbolic poll protesting government plans to house hundreds of asylum seekers at a nearby former air force base. The vote in Barnham follows a similar protest referendum in the village of Piddington in September, also over government plans to move asylum seekers from hotels into former military accommodation. Between 400 to 500 people were eligible to vote in the ballot which carried no legal weight, with 257 voting for independence, 16 against, and one spoilt ballot. “There’s an issue with the sheer volume of people expected to be accommodated,” the chairwoman of the Barnham residents’ association, Helen Beck, told AFP earlier. “Barnham is a small village. There will be nothing for the (lodged) people to do, nowhere to go.” Under plans by Britain’s government, the base near the village in rural eastern England will be used to accommodate 931 migrants. The village has a population of 584. Residents were asked whether they supported seeking a “crown dependency status” similar to that of Jersey, Guernsey and the Isle of Man. Parish council chair John Bauer said this would allow the village to “retain loyalty to the crown” while removing itself from Home Office jurisdiction. – Safety concern – Residents in both Barnham and Piddington say they are also worried about locals’ safety, particularly that of women. “We’ve been told they (the asylum seekers) are all males. We don’t know where they are from, their background,” Beck said. “People are anxious about walking alone, walking their dog in darkness if an additional 900 men arrive in the area,” she said. In the Piddington vote in September, 285 out of 312 votes were cast in favour of “pursuing self-determination”. The government plans to house around 1,250 asylum seekers on a former defence ministry site close to Piddington village, all single men between 18 and 65. Britain’s centre-left government, in power since July 2024, has vowed to end the use of hotels as migrant accommodation following a public outcry. It plans to move all those currently in hotels — a policy inherited from the last Conservative government — to former military bases by 2029. But Beck said that there were questions about whether military-style accommodation was suitable for people “fleeing a conflict or persecution”, adding that it was also “significantly more expensive than hotels”. nigeria.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”. But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in the country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960. Today, Nigeria, like many countries on the continent with limited education budgets, has a hard enough time placing children in dedicated schools for the deaf and hard of hearing. And there’s even less attention paid to local sign languages used outside the school system — a serious disservice to the country’s linguistic diversity, Festus Zenda, who has worked on documentation projects with local deaf communities, told AFP. “These indigenous signing systems should be studied, documented and preserved before changes in education, migration, technology and wider use of Nigerian Sign Language cause some of them to decline or disappear,” said Zenda, who has helped document the local sign language used by the Tiv ethnic group, in Benue state. A deaf resident gestures with his fingers while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Displacement by formal signing The working-class Abuja exurb of Zuba is a symphony of motorcycle horns, plantain hawkers’ shouts and the dull hum of construction work. Another group adds their own, milder contributions: claps, muffled shouts of exclamation and the swish of rapid hand gestures as they chat in Hausa signs. nigeria.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
nigeria.description: African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present. Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate. The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations. CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing. CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup. “Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said. “I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.” Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer. Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal. “You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects. On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. “He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said. McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc. “There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said. “There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands. “This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally.” The post Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino appeared first on Vanguard News .

Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X. A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported. “Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said. They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said. Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low. Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022. Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory. Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported. Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported. Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600. Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. "Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession," said a Fifpro statement. "Contracts are there to be respected. sports.description: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin admitted that he lacked speed in the Portuguese Grand Prix sprint, suggesting he owes his slim MotoGP title hopes entirely to Marc Marquez ’s crash. The factory Aprilia rider arrived at Portimao needing to outscore Marquez by 24 points over the weekend to take the championship fight to the Valencia finale. But after qualifying five places behind Marquez in seventh, Martin failed to make any headway in the sprint, gaining only one position in the opening 10 laps. That would have let Marquez seal the title with a third-place finish, but the Ducati star crashed out of the sprint on the penultimate tour as rain began to fall on the track. Speaking afterwards, Martin admitted that he was lagging behind the frontrunners at Portimao, particularly with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi converting pole position into a dominant win. Asked whether he had kept his championship hopes alive, Martin insisted the outcome was never in his hands given the points situation. “Well, I didn't ‘keep’ anything. Everything was in Marc's hands,” he said. “For sure, it was a really tricky race. I didn't have the speed all weekend. Finally, in the race, it seemed I found a little bit extra. I was quite close to the podium fight, but I missed a bit more speed. “But in the end, I did my best. I finished in fifth position. Let's hope for a bigger improvement tomorrow. “When the conditions are really tricky like this, the focus more goes on riding because you need to be at 100%. “So you don't have room to think about anything. sports.title: Nick Saban names his top national championship contenders, and Alabama isn’t one of them
sports.description: Jul 22, 2026; Tampa, FL, USA; former Alabama Crimson Tide coach and ESPN analyst for College GameDay Nick Saban broadcast during SEC Football Kickoff Media Day at the Tampa Marriott. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images With just a couple of weeks left in the regular season, the College Football Playoff picture is starting to come into focus. And one of the most decorated coaches in the sport’s history thinks that only a few teams have what it takes to win it all. Former Alabama head coach Nick Saban said on Friday that there are “three teams that have the right stuff” to win the national championship: Georgia, Utah, and Notre Dame. And despite spending more than two decades coaching in the SEC, he made sure to clarify that it was “no disrespect to Alabama.” Playoff Picture Taking Shape Georgia sits at No. 1 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings at 9-1, with its only loss coming against Auburn in October. The Bulldogs have won three straight since then, including a 48-21 win over Missouri last weekend. Utah is right behind at No. 2 and is one of two undefeated teams in the top five at 10-0, along with No. 4 UCLA, though the Utes needed a 40-39 win at Arizona last weekend to keep their perfect season alive. Notre Dame checks in at No. 6 at 9-1, with its only loss coming at BYU. The Fighting Irish have since won three straight, including a 31-24 win over Miami. Georgia quarterback Gunner Stockton and Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr were both named finalists for the Johnny Unitas Golden Arm Award on Friday, according to On3. On the same show, Saban insisted that the SEC is still the best conference from top to bottom, despite the Big Ten winning three straight national titles. Yet only one of his three contenders plays in the SEC. ‘The right stuff’ Saban shared his picks during Friday’s appearance on The Pat McAfee Show . “I think there’s three teams that have the right stuff. And this is no disrespect to Alabama, because I think there’s probably seven to eight teams that can win the championship, Alabama being one of them. But if you’re a betting man and you say, ‘OK, who can run the ball, who can play good defense and who has a good quarterback?’ You would say Georgia has that, Utah has that, Notre Dame has that,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban added that the rest of the contenders have weaknesses that could hold them back. “Everybody else maybe has a flaw somewhere along the way. Now they might be able to overcome it, but I think those three teams have the right stuff,” Saban said. That leaves out Alabama, which the committee has ranked No. 3, as well as No. 4 UCLA, No. 5 Texas, and No. 7 Miami, among others. Clearly, Saban thinks the national title race is a lot narrower than the rankings suggest. sports.title: Redick Fires Up Lakers After Listless First Half vs. Kings
sports.description: May 7, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick yells to his team during a play against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the first half during game two of the second round of the 2026 NBA Playoffs at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images The Lakers did not look like a championship team for the first 24 minutes on Friday. They looked flat against the last-place Sacramento Kings, trailing by eight points at the break. Coach JJ Redick had seen enough and decided to get loud . He did not sugarcoat the message to his squad in the locker room. “I feel I did a decent job of regulating at halftime… They may have a differing opinion of that. Can’t repeat every word I used,” Redick said after the team secured a narrow 106-104 win . The coach admitted his words were harsh but necessary to wake the players up. A Wake-Up Call for the Big Men Redick’s anger was not aimed at everyone equally. He zeroed in on center Walker Kessler , who had just six points, one rebound, and four fouls before the break. The coach told Kessler to be tougher and bring some energy. Kessler did not argue with the approach, noting that Reddick tore into him about it, and rightfully so. The player admitted he was not playing physically or going to the rim. He needed that push to find his game. Kessler finished with 15 points and seven rebounds after the halftime talk. He credited the coach for knowing when to yell. The contrast between the two big men was stark. While Kessler struggled early, Kings star Domantas Sabonis dominated with 15 points and eight boards. The Lakers could not let that happen again. Redick made sure they understood the stakes. “The main message was we’ve got to be tougher, we’ve got to bring a little bit of energy,” Redick explained. He noted that some players might have a different opinion of his halftime speech. He would not repeat every word he used, but the point was clear. Stars Back the Coach’s Approach Even the biggest stars on the roster agreed with the coach’s methods. Luka Doncic led the team with 25 points and eight assists. He said the yelling helped get everyone fired up. “I mean, he yells, but I’m used to it,” Doncic said. He noted that sometimes it is good to have a coach who demands more. The team managed to outscore Sacramento 52-42 over the final two quarters. That second-half surge kept them from losing to a team with a 1-14 record. The game came down to the final second. Sacramento guard Zach LaVine had a chance to win it with a three-pointer at the buzzer. The shot clanked off the front rim, and the Lakers survived. The win lifted L.A. to 14-3 on the season. It was their second win in NBA Cup games. The victory was sweet, but the performance was far from perfect . The team has now survived close calls against weaker opponents all week. Per ESPN , the Lakers needed a 47-point night from Quentin Grimes to beat the Hornets on Tuesday. Redick knows that scraping by is not enough for a top seed.

sports.title: ‘There’s a bigger issue people just don’t get’: Metta World Peace claps back after Stephen A. Smith’s racial Laker comments
sports.description: Jan 7, 2020; Los Angeles, California, USA; Metta World Peace (Ron Artest) attends a game between the Los Angeles Lakers and the New York Knicks at Staples Center. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Los Angeles Lakers sit at the top of the Western Conference at 14-3, just ahead of the 13-3 San Antonio Spurs, despite losing superstar veteran LeBron James. European sensation Luka Doncic has firmly secured the reins of the team and is aiming to be an NBA scoring champ at the pace he’s playing. But the new roster selection has received criticism from some of sports’ most acclaimed commentators despite their hot start. After James left in free agency this offseason, the Lakers’ new-look roster drew plenty of reaction, especially from ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith, who couldn’t picture three white guys winning an NBA title in today’s league. But between Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler, the trio has averaged 76.2 points, 20.8 rebounds, and 14.2 assists per game. Recently, on First Take , Smith doubled down on his thoughts while openly asking “the brothers” around the league to step up and stop the Lakers, creating a media spiral of its own . Wednesday, former Lakers champion Metta World Peace pushed back against Smith’s take, making it clear he has zero issue with a white-run team. “I love seeing white basketball players on same team,” World Peace wrote via X . “I feel no less insecure about a majority white @Lakers. That’s like saying you are afraid of a black mom and black dad born president. People are so unaware that they are ignitors of racism. That’s like saying, my new semi chip company will not succeed because I’m a black board member. Let the white ball players rock and let our future black financial system principals and my new social impact go to market concepts rock.” Friday, in a video posted by Bassey on X , World Peace continued to defend his positioning but deepened the outlook as he believes there are other underlying issues that have been “brewing for years” in the NBA. “There’s a bigger issue that people just don’t get in terms of us players that are dope in sports. We charge for training,” World Peace added. “So now one of the issues is that a lot of us that’s out of poverty cannot afford even our services that came from poverty, which is why we do a lot of free work. So there are a lot of, you know, ethnic, you know, kind of, cultured individuals of the same ethnicity as myself that’s not getting the same training, because they can’t afford it.” It is not unusual for Smith’s comments to cause such an uproar, but his reaction will be interesting to see given that he has had a heavy political schedule for the past few months. sports.title: Oregon men's cross country misses NCAA podium by single point
sports.description: The Oregon men fell one-point short of ending their long NCAA Cross Country Championships trophy drought. Led by a pair of all-American performances from Nick Griggs and Simeon Birnbaum, the Ducks scored 196 points as a team to finish in fifth place Nov. 21 at on the LaVern Gibson Championship Course in Terre Haute, Ind. BYU was fourth with 195 points, leaving Oregon off the podium for an 11th straight year. Griggs made his Ducks’ and NCAA debut Saturday, finishing the 10,000-meter race in ninth place in 28:45.7. Birnbaum was 23rd in 29:05.1. Oregon’s next scorer was Myles Hogan, who was 65th in 29:36.5, followed by Aiden Smith, who was 70th in 29:41.0 and Benjamin Balazs, who was 79th in 29:48.4. Also on the course for the Ducks were Tayson Echohawk (93rd in 29:57.4) and Evan Jenkins (205th in 31:00.0). Louisville’s Elsingi Kipruto took home the individual title with a 28:27.7 finish. New Mexico, with three runners finishing in the top 10 and four in the top 14, won the team title with 69 points. Colorado was second with 107 and Alabama third with 109. Oregon women finish ninth The Ducks had a pair of finishers in the top 25, but there was a big gap between them and their other scorers as Oregon scored 312 points to finish in ninth place. Diana Cherotich was Oregon’s top runner as the Big Ten champ finished the 6,000-meter race in 17th place in 19:06.8. Juliet Cherubet wasn’t far behind as she finished in 21st in 19:10.9. Both runners earned all-American status – a third such honor for Cherubet and second for Cherotich. Dalia Frias finished in 58th (19:37.3), Ella Thorsett was 108th (20:08.8) and Ava Parekh was 185th (20:46.5). Finishing outside of scoring was Kendall Martin, who was 246th in 21:34.9. Sofia Thogersen, who had been the Ducks’ No. 4 runner all season, started but didn’t finish the race. Hannah Grapes of NC State was the individual winner in 18:44.3. Alabama won the team title with 120 points, West Virginia was second at 145, BYU was third with 152, and Northern Arizona was fourth with 215. sports.title: Stampede Blue Reacts results (Week 12): Colts fan confidence falls to 12% as frustration reaches new low
sports.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 15: Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon of the Indianapolis Colts takes the field prior to an NFL football game between the Miami Dolphins and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to this week’s SB Nation Reacts survey, just 12 percent of Colts fans believe the team is headed in the right direction . That number marks another sharp drop in fan confidence and shows just how bleak things have become in Indianapolis. At this point, the overwhelming majority of the fan base appears to have little belief in the current direction of the franchise. The continued decline in confidence is hardly surprising. The Colts have spent the past several weeks spiraling, and whatever optimism may have briefly surfaced after some of the front office changes has quickly disappeared. Poor offensive play, frustrating coaching decisions and the overall lack of progress from week to week have left fans with very little reason to feel encouraged. Rather than showing signs of a team building toward something, Indianapolis has looked like a franchise stuck in the middle of a messy transition. The biggest recent development, of course, is that Daniel Jones is now gone, officially closing the book on a move that never gave the Colts the boost they were hoping for. Jones had a few respectable moments early on, but the offense became increasingly dysfunctional under his watch, and it eventually reached a point where a change simply had to be made. His departure does not solve all of Indianapolis’ problems, but it does signal that the organization recognized the situation was no longer tenable. Even so, the quarterback change alone is unlikely to restore confidence overnight. The issues with this team go far beyond one player. Shane Steichen continues to face questions about the offense, the roster still has major holes, and the Colts remain far away from looking like a legitimate contender. At the same time, fans are now left wondering whether this next phase will at least provide some clarity about the future, even if the short-term results remain ugly. For now, this week’s 12 percent confidence mark says it all. Colts fans are not just frustrated, they are increasingly unconvinced that this franchise has a real plan in place. If Indianapolis wants that number to rise in the coming weeks, it will need to show something far more convincing than it has lately. sports.title: Aston Villa frustrated by Sunderland in dull goalless draw
sports.description: Aston Villa and Sunderland drew a blank in their Premier League match at Villa Park. Unai Emery’s team had the better of a game of few chances but failed to make the breakthrough and are now without a win in five games in all competitions. Sunderland, bidding to move away from the relegation zone, ended a run of three successive away defeats with the 0-0 draw. Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Emiliano Buendia returned for Villa at the expense of Victor Lindelof and John McGinn , who was on the bench. Sunderland also made two changes, with Jules Ahoka and Wilson Isidor replacing the injured Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey. The home side were on the front foot from the off and forced a couple of early corners, which came to nothing. They had to wait until the 19th minute for their first chance, with Johan Manzambi’s low effort saved by Robin Roefs. The Sunderland goalkeeper had a let-off in the 40th minute when he gifted possession to Buendia but recovered to claim the Villa midfielder’s weak shot. Ian Maatsen threatened to break the deadlock in the early stages of the second half, but he could only follow an impressive run with a shot straight at Roefs. Soon after the Black Cats, who created little of note before half-time, forced their first corner but failed to produce anything worthwhile from it. Villa’s Leon Goretzka was then booked for pulling back Chemsdine Talbi, but Enzo Le Fee’s free-kick evaded Nordi Mukiele and was collected by goalkeeper Zion Suzuki. As Villa fans chanted for the introduction of McGinn, Le Fee fired narrowly wide. The home faithful got what they wanted just before the hour mark when McGinn was introduced, alongside Ibrahim Mbaye. The Scotland international had a chance to open the scoring midway through the second half but fired over. Sunderland won a free-kick 25 yards out when Goretzka fouled Le Fee, but the midfielder’s effort was straight at Suzuki. Villa boss Emery made another double substitution in the 73rd minute, with Brian Madjo and Ross Barkley replacing Nicolas Jackson and Goretzka. The home side pressed for a winner and, after McGinn failed to find the target three minutes later, Barkley forced Roefs to tip over a powerful effort from distance. Roefs reacted sharply to prevent Mukiele heading into his own goal, then Alysson fired over. The visitors almost stole a win in the first of three added minutes, but Talbi’s curling right-foot effort went narrowly wide of Suzuki’s far post.

sports.title: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo
sports.description: ‘Phase 3’ of Real Madrid’s season under Mourinho gets underway against Celta Vigo Jose Mourinho’s influence on the Real Madrid dressing room and slowly, yet surely grown, and the player now appear more hungry and prepared to win than they have in recent years. The opening phase of the season, which lasted until the first international break, saw Los Blancos adapt to Mourinho’s ways and even struggle to rack up wins. They were often dominated and scraped through games, which was understandable. After the first international break, however, matters changed for the good and the men in white began to look increasingly convincing. They began controlling games better and performing consistently, with the Clasico win marking their highest point. Phase 3 begins Mourinho has got Real Madrid back on track. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) As reported by AS in a recent update, Mourinho sees the new phase of the season that lies ahead of of the team as their third phase, and he is hoping for an even better run. By the time Christmas arrives, the manager hopes that Los Blancos are playing better football and that they have the UEFA Champions League qualification in the bag. If possible, he even hopes for a change on the league leaderboard with his side going on top. Mourinho’s plans have been moving as expected so far, but the manager is aware that the project is just getting started and that there is a long way to go. He has even proclaimed that reaching perfection will require ‘three seasons.’ Big games ahead Real Madrid have unpleasant memories of playing against Arsenal heading into next month’s clash. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Between the game against Celta Vigo tonight and the end of the year, Real Madrid have some big games to get past, and the third phase will be more challenging than one anticipates. For starters, Los Blancos will take on PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League after the clash against Celta Vigo, and will then go on a challenging three away-game streak. First, they must travel to Anoeta where they must take on Real Sociedad, and they then travel to San Mames for a clash against Real Sociedad. Both games, needless to say, are difficult outings and bring back unfavourable memories. Then, Mourinho and Co. must take on Arsenal away from home – a game that will bring back ghosts of the past. After all, they lost 3-0 at the venue – one of their biggest European defeats in recent times.

sports.title: Bournemouth climb up to fourth after securing ninth victory in a row
sports.description: Bournemouth extended their winning run to nine in all competitions as Evanilson scored for the sixth Premier League game in a row in a 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest. Justin Kluivert was also on target to help Marco Rose’s Cherries climb up to the dizzying heights of fourth place in the table. The defeat means Forest are only above the relegation places on goal difference having failed to build on the momentum of their 3-1 win over Manchester City before the international break. Both teams started the game on the front foot and Forest had the first sight of goal. Neco Williams nodded dangerously across the face of goal at the far post, but Liam Delap was beaten to the ball by home defender Antonio Silva. Evanilson was denied by a brilliant last-ditch tackle from Forest centre-back Jair Cunha before Marcus Tavernier’s 20-yard curler was well saved by Matz Sels. Bournemouth took the lead through Evanilson in the 19th minute. James Hill cushioned a header into the path of Evanilson, and the in-form Brazilian took one touch before blasting a left-footed shot into the roof of the net. Evanilson (centre) celebrates the opening goal (Steven Paston/PA) (PA Wire) Kluivert almost doubled the home side’s lead with an effort from the edge of the penalty area which sailed narrowly over the crossbar. Evanilson then failed to keep his shot down after a long throw from Hill caused chaos in the Forest penalty area. Oliver Glasner’s side had a penalty appeal waved away when Adam Smith blocked Williams’s effort into the arm of team-mate Tyler Adams. Kluivert did make it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time with a simple far-post finish after a superb run and cross from Tavernier. Forest were much improved in the second half, adopting a more direct approach in a bid to forage a way back into the game. Delap turned provider by whipping in a cross for captain Morgan Gibbs-White but the England international could not properly connect with his header. James McAtee ballooned an effort over the crossbar as the visitors continued to misfire in front of goal. Substitute Chris Wood also miscued a header from a corner when he should have at least tested underworked Bournemouth goalkeeper Dorde Petrovic. Bournemouth always looked a threat on the counter and Kluivert came close to his second and the Cherries’ third when he stung the gloves of Selz from 18 yards out. Kluivert should also have been more clinical when he found himself within finishing range but unselfishly laid the ball off to Rayan and the chance went begging.

technology.title: AWS got hit by an outage too. Here's why you didn't hear about it
technology.description: My editor asked me this week "why is everything except AWS breaking?" It's a great question! They haven't been in the headlines! In fact, as they are wont to do, AWS spokesperson Patrick Neighorn g ot salty to a reporter about how unreliable Downdetector is when it started showing them as impacted. If you'll permit me a small digression, this stems from a misunderstanding of what Downdetector is for. Historically the AWS status site was so hilariously slow to reflect the lived customer experience that some jackass (me) built a rewriter that sits at stop.lying.cloud to make it a smidgen more realistic. As a result, the question people are really trying to answer when they visit Downdetector is "my app just broke; is it my crappy code or is there a global event going on?" There are mitigations for both, but they look nothing alike. AWS view crowdsourced reports of the form "the internet is broken, must be AWS" as a stain upon their honor. In fact, it's a badge of their own success, as "the internet" and "AWS" have become inextricably linked in people's minds. But back to my editor's question, "why didn't AWS go down?" Easy: it did. Everything breaks, all the time, including the narrative AWS now has 34 generally available commercial regions, of which two are currently smoking craters due to the Iran conflict. Each of these has hundreds of services that AWS offers to customers, of which a dozen or so are high quality, if I'm being characteristically uncharitable. They experience degradation in various ways, and they go largely unnoticed. But on November 15, AWS confirmed an incident that disrupted 11 of those ~12 good services in their oldest and most important region, us-east-1. At 3:05 AM PST, they stated that they started seeing sign-up errors, authentication issues, and connectivity issues. Five minutes later engineers were engaged. Not to be outdone, their status page swung into action after a leisurely coffee, and posted its first indication of an incident 93 minutes later. (See previous comments on stop.lying.cloud ). The all-clear showed up at 6:53 AM. Every site has downtime. Sometimes it blows up publicly, other times nobody seems to notice. Heck, AWS said in September that it had experienced permanent data loss in its two smoking craters, but after that news cycle passed I haven't heard a thing about it. I do think it's patently unreasonable to blame them for this specific problem; "acts of war" are kinda hard to predict from the corporate planning meeting. A few things combined to help AWS out on November 15. First, it was pre-dawn Pacific time on Sunday. Most of us slept through it; my kids aren't even up that early. Further, the services that were most impacted (IAM Identity Center) were for engineers signing in to AWS accounts, not consumers staring at an app that stopped working. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
science.description: null On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule. Rømer figured out the pattern and made an accurate prediction for Io's eclipse on Nov. 9, 1676. Then on Nov. 21, he took his findings to the Royal Academy of Sciences and explained that a finite speed of light must be responsible. Danish astronomer Ole Rømer (Image credit: Wikimedia Commons) Why it mattered Understanding that the speed of light is a constant is the key that opened our ability to gauge the scale of the universe, as well as was central to developing modern physics. "The speed of light becomes a sort of ultimate speed limit," Live Science explained in an article about why the speed of light matters. "In fact, objects with mass, be they cars or neutrinos, can't reach the speed of light because they would need infinite energy to do so."
